_readme: Where each page's first chart begins, in CSS pixels from the top of the document at
1440x900. The house rule is that a reader meets evidence in the first screen; a page
that opens on 1,800px of prose has broken it, and until 2026-08-28 fifteen of sixteen
pages had, with no check looking.
This file is a RATCHET, not a target. A page listed here may only improve: the gate
fails if its first chart moves further down than the number recorded. Pages fixed to
the rule carry the LIMIT (900) rather than their measured value, so they cannot drift
back. A page NOT listed here must clear 900 outright, which is what makes this safe
for new pages.
The unfixed numbers are debts, recorded honestly rather than hidden behind a
threshold nobody meets. Lower them as pages are fixed.
PLATFORM, added 2026-09-01. Every number here was measured on macOS. On that day CI
began running this gate for the first time (it had run four of the twenty gates until
then), and four pages measured 3 to 40px higher on the Linux runner: text wraps
differently, so the prose above the first chart is a line or two taller. The numbers
below are now the LINUX measurements, because CI is the platform that enforces them and
a ratchet enforced on one platform and calibrated on another is not a ratchet.
A local macOS run will therefore read comfortably under every entry. That is a real
weakness: a Mac-only regression of up to ~40px would pass locally and be caught only on
push. The fix is to make rendering deterministic across platforms rather than to
re-measure per platform, which means launching chromium with font hinting and subpixel
positioning disabled. That changes the measurement basis of nine pixel-measuring gates
at once, so it is filed as its own change (LEDGER ER-021) rather than ridden in here.
